item.title: [直接·合成氨] Can existing or future pathways reduce green ammonia production costs?
item.description:
ChemRxiv · 2026-10-29 · 合成氨
N₂/H₂气相合成氨｜未交代供热方式

Many scenarios for the energy transition consider green ammonia. The technologically most mature production process combines water electrolysis and Haber-Bosch process (EHB). Its costs are dominated by electrolyzer investment costs and electricity. Emerging pathways researched in academia, start-ups, and industry try to reduce costs by changing sub-processes and chemistry. However, it remains unclear which pathways have the potential to outperform EHB, if any. We assess relevant emerging pathways, compare to EHB in terms of costs and energy demand, and derive performance targets. Many pathways investigated in the literature, such as metalmediated electrolysis, have theoretical minimal energy demands well above the actual energy demand of EHB; consequently, they cannot produce ammonia at competitive costs due to the high influence of electricity costs. Any novel pathway must employ simple and energy-effective chemistry to substantially reduce costs. Identified performance targets are applicable to novel pathways and can guide research, industry, and policy makers.

item.title: [⭐交叉·合成氨] Oxygen Vacancy Engineering Unlocks Efficient Ammonia Synthesis Over Rare-Earth-Modified Ru/CeO2
item.description:
Energy & Fuels · 2026-10-17 · 合成氨
N₂/H₂气相合成氨；涉及Ru/钌体系｜表征温程（TPR/TPD/TPO 等，不等于反应供热）

Abstract Rare-earth engineering of CeO2 offers a route to enhance Ru-based catalysts for ammonia synthesis by tailoring oxygen vacancies and metal–support interactions. Herein, we systematically synthesized and benchmarked Ru catalysts supported on RE (=Gd, La, and Sm)-modified CeO2 under identical conditions to establish promoter-structure–activity relationships. Rare-earth incorporation increased the Ce3+/Ce4+ ratio, oxygen-vacancy concentration, and weak acidic sites, facilitating electron transfer to Ru, promoting N2 activation, and potentially facilitating interfacial hydrogen spillover. H2-TPD suggested improved hydrogen mobility and utilization at the Ru/CeO2 interface. Ru/GdCeO exhibited the highest NH3 synthesis rate of (19.80 ± 0.98) mmol g–1h–1 at 400 °C and 1.5 MPa, with an N2:H2 ratio of 1:2 and WHSV = 13,500 mL g–1 h–1, yielding 3.53 vol % NH3 in the reactor effluent. Such superior performance may be associated with optimized Ru-support interactions and abundant oxygen vacancies. These findings establish Gd as the most effective promoter for Ru/CeO2 under mild synthesis conditions.

item.description:

Abstract Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions

item.title: [直接·合成氨] Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
item.description:
Journal of the American Chemical Society · 2026-10-10 · 合成氨
制氨路线未明确；涉及Ru/钌体系｜未交代供热方式

Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

Abstract Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions remains challenging because of the inertness of the N≡N bond and the limited ability of conventional catalysts to couple efficient dinitrogen activation with rapid hydrogenation. Here, we report a LiH/FePcG catalyst in which strong interfacial coupling between LiH and Fe–N–C sites enable efficient ammonia synthesis. Comprehensive characterization, including structural analysis, kinetic study, isotopic-labelling, gas-phase mass spectrometry, and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) reveal that the catalytic activity originates from interfacial active sites. Under reaction conditions, structural nitrogen atoms within the Fe–Nx moieties undergo reversible consumption and reconstruction, demonstrating the dynamic participation of the Fe–N–C framework in ammonia synthesis. Concurrently, hydridic hydrogen supplied by LiH directly participates in the initial hydrogenation steps, while the LiH/Fe–N–C interface generates Fe-centered multicomponent hydride species essential for N2 binding and activation. As the global energy sector transitions toward net-zero emissions, kraft pulp mills present a compelling opportunity to produce green fuels and achieve net-negative emissions by capturing biogenic carbon, helping offset hard-to-abate sectors. This study explores the techno-economics of integrating biomass gasification for green ammonia production within kraft mills, using KraftSIM modeling to evaluate ammonia production, steam balance, emissions, and utility impacts. The proposed design enables energy and water system integration with the existing mill and allows for a gradual scale-up without disrupting the chemistry and operation of the recovery cycle. Uranium nitrides UN 2− x are excellent candidates as catalyst for ammonia synthesis, as demonstrated by their historical precedent. However, despite their potential, uranium nitrides have not been extensively investigated. In this study, we theoretically investigated the bulk and surface properties of pure and defective UN 2 (UN 1.75 ) implementing DFT + U approach. Uranium nitride UN 2 is not stable, and vacancies are spontaneously formed leading to N/U ratio between 1.7 and 1.8 depending on the synthesis conditions. The vacancy formation energy of UN 2 was calculated as −0.70 eV. To identify the most stable surface, surface energy was calculated for both UN 2 and UN 1.75 catalyst built in four Miller indices (100), (110), (111), and (121). It was found that (111) surface is the most stable one. Moreover, considering differences in distribution of vacancies in UN 1.75 , a random vacancy distribution for (111) surface shows the lower surface energy of 0.51 J.m −2 . The surface can easily be covered by layer of oxygen at very low oxygen pressure even at high temperature of 1500 K. An amorphous CuNiAgCe medium-entropy metallic glass was synthesized via ultrafast pulsed Joule heating for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia. The abundant synergistic active sites on its surface establish a novel tandem catalytic pathway that successfully decouples linear scaling relationships. As a result, the catalyst delivers a remarkable ammonia yield rate of 520.86 µmol h-1 cm-2 and a faradaic efficiency of 99.72% at a low potential of -0.3 V vs. RHE. This work offers new insights into the design and construction of next-generation tandem synergistic catalytic sites.

Herein, Bi-containing coal tar pitch-derived carbon nanofibers (CTP-TU-Bi) were prepared by electrospinning, pre-oxidation, and Joule heating and directly used as flexible binder-free anodes for sodium-ion batteries. Joule heating was used to convert the electrospun precursor into a continuous carbon nanofiber framework containing crystalline Bi nanoparticles. Microscopy and XPS results support the formation of Bi-C interfaces and changes in the local chemical environment. Density functional theory calculations based on simplified carbon and Bi-containing models indicate more favorable Na adsorption and a lower calculated Na migration barrier in the Bi-containing model. Keywords: Joule heating; Complex hydrocarbon mixtures; Light olefins; Spatiotemporal reactor; Reaction-separation mechanism Introduction Light olefins are essential building blocks for the chemical industry, and expanding their production from diverse hydrocarbon mixtures is important for improving resource utilization and securing olefin supply. Complex carbonaceous resources, including waste plastics, petroleum, and coal liquefaction products, represent abundant feedstocks for light olefin production. Industrially, light olefins are produced mainly through steam cracking and catalytic pyrolysis.1, 2, 3 These processes rely heavily on fossil fuel combustion for heat supply, resulting in high energy consumption and carbon emissions.4 It poses a major challenge to the low-carbon transition of olefin production technology. Thus, developing low-carbon heat supply strategies while maintaining high olefin selectivity is critical for next-generation olefin production technologies.

ABSTRACT The regeneration of graphite anodes from spent lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for sustainable battery recycling. Existing strategies typically rely on energy‐intensive graphitization or hazardous chemical treatments, which are either ineffective in repairing intrinsic defects or environmentally unsustainable. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) has emerged as a powerful fabrication strategy for the design of advanced electrocatalysts for water electrolysis. Owing to its sequential self‐limiting surface reactions, ALD enables atomic‐scale control over film thickness, composition, morphology, and interface structure, while simultaneously providing highly conformal coatings on complex and porous substrates. These characteristics make ALD particularly attractive for engineering electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER), where catalyst utilization, stability, and interface properties critically influence electrochemical performance. Beyond catalyst synthesis, ALD has also emerged as a powerful platform for disentangling structure‐activity‐stability relationships in electrocatalysis. This review discusses recent advances in ALD‐enabled electrocatalyst fabrication for water electrolysis, with emphasis on noble‐metal and earth‐abundant catalyst systems, including transition‐metal oxides, sulfides, and phosphides. item.title: [可迁移·焦耳热] Synergistic Core–Satellite Interfacial Nanoarchitectonics via Ultrafast Microwave Joule Heating for Durable Zn Anodes With Enhanced Ion Kinetics
item.description:
ChemSusChem · 2026-10-27 · 焦耳热
析氢反应｜反应阶段焦耳/电阻供热

The commercialization of Zn metal anodes is constrained by dendrite growth and severe side reactions, despite their low cost and high volumetric capacity. Herein, we leverage the microwave‐induced skin effect to establish the hybrid interphase layer by sequentially incorporating Zn 2+ ‐affinitive Cu and HER‐suppressive Bi. The in situ formed protective layer, composed of core–satellite nanoarchitectonics, exhibits a thin and gradient feature owing to the limited penetration depth of electromagnetic energy via ultrafast Joule heating. The introduction of Cu species evolves into CuZn 5 alloy microsphere cores, which bond intimately to the Zn substrate with minimum lattice mismatch, thereby facilitating uniform Zn nucleation and dense deposition. Meanwhile, the confined growth of nanosized Bi satellites effectively suppresses parasitic reactions, endowing the Zn anode with a prolonged lifespan exceeding 3400 h at 5 mA cm −2 . The full cell employing the modified Zn anode and NaV 3 O 8 cathode demonstrates excellent capacity retention of 86% after 1000 cycles at 2 A g −1 .

Abstract The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. Abstract Practical direct air capture (DAC) demands a sorbent contactor that simultaneously delivers high active-material loading, low flow resistance, efficient mass transfer, and rapid regeneration─requirements that conventional sorbent architectures rarely satisfy together. Here, we present a woven fiber contactor that addresses these requirements by interlacing dry-fabricated zeolite Y/PTFE fibers with copper wire supports into a structured contactor. Compared to a stacked laminate configuration, the woven sorbent exhibited markedly more efficient mass transfer, yielding a narrower mass transfer zone (LMTZ = 4.4 mm and 11.1 mm at 50 sccm) and a steeper breakthrough front. Abstract Microwave-driven carbothermal shock (CTS) synthesis has attracted considerable attention as an ultrafast route for nanomaterial production. However, controlling nanoparticle nucleation and growth during the extremely short microwave irradiation period remains challenging. Although defect-rich carbon materials have frequently been employed in microwave-driven CTS synthesis, the influence of a separately introduced defect-containing surface layer on nanoparticle formation remains insufficiently understood. item.description:
Chemistry Letters · 2026-10-06 · 焦耳热
过程待核实｜电化学驱动，不等于床层焦耳热

Abstract A rapid, energy-saving Fe/N/C oxygen reduction reaction catalyst was prepared by sequential induction heating and microwave irradiation. Compared with electric-furnace treatments, the process reduced heat-treatment time and electrical energy consumption by 87% and 78%, respectively. The enhanced oxygen reduction reaction activity was attributed to an increase in Fe–Nx and pyridinic-N species and to suppressed growth of large Fe-containing particles. The catalyst also retained its oxygen reduction reaction activity in methanol-containing electrolyte, demonstrating promise for direct methanol fuel-cell cathodes.

Phosphorus-containing hybrid organic-inorganic materials demonstrate unique physicochemical properties making them suitable candidates for energy storage, electrocatalysis, and as protective and biocompatible coatings. Of special interest in this regard are metal phosphonate films, where the organic group bound to the P atom can tune functional properties of the films. However, the deposition of such materials in thin-film form remains challenging and has achieved only limited success. In this work, we present two deposition processes employing combination of atomic and molecular layer deposition approaches for the growth of aluminium phosphonates, utilizing trimethylaluminum as the Al source, and dimethyl methylphosphonate and dimethyl phenylphosphonate as the P sources, respectively. Both processes demonstrated saturated growth, and the incorporation of the phosphonate groups was confirmed using ex situ x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Although catalytic wet peroxide oxidation (CWPO) effectively remediates organic wastewater, high reagent requirements and slow reaction kinetics limit its practical application. Here, a core-shell Fe3O4@ZIF‒67 catalyst (FOZIF) was synthesized and used in an induction heating-assisted CWPO (IH‒CWPO) system for the rapid and efficient generation of reactive radicals. In this system, induction heating synergistically accelerates H2O2 activation over the FOZIF catalyst to generate abundant hydroxyl radicals. Mechanistically, the electron-donating Fe2+ species in the Fe3O4 core accelerate the Co3+/Co2+ redox cycle within the ZIF-67 shell, establishing a dual Fe/Co active site network. Consequently, the optimized FOZIF‒2 catalyst achieved 98.2% degradation of tetracycline (TC) within 30 min in the IH‒CWPO system, yielding a remarkable rate constant of 1.46 × 10−1 min−1, significantly outperforming conventional CWPO. item.title: [可迁移·焦耳热] Flash Joule heating-induced oxygen-deficient TiO2 for high-rate lithium storage
item.description:
SSRN · 2026-10-06 · 焦耳热
材料制备/结构调控；涉及碳材料｜焦耳热用于制备

The low electronic conductivity of TiO2 limits its rate capability as a lithium-ion battery anode. Conductive TiO2 was prepared from commercial anatase powder by carbon-cloth-assisted flash Joule heating (FJH). Conductivity increased with treatment temperature and pulse number, reaching 24.32 S cm−1 after 100 pulses at 1500 °C. The resulting material was predominantly rutile. X-ray photoelectron and electron paramagnetic resonance spectra supported oxygen vacancy formation and partial Ti reduction, which may contribute to the increased conductivity. The apparent optical bandgap decreased from 3.30 to 2.02 eV. In lithium half-cells, the treated material delivered approximately 62 mAh g−1 at 20 C and maintained approximately 80 mAh g−1 after 400 cycles at 10 C.

Selective catalytic conversion of complex hydrocarbons into light olefins remains challenging because of costly catalyst preparation and catalyst deactivation under severe cracking conditions. Here, we report pulsed Joule heating for highly selective light olefin production from complex hydrocarbon mixtures. By precisely regulating reaction severity, this catalyst-free approach achieves light olefin yields comparable to those reported for catalytic cracking. We systematically characterized the feedstock molecular composition and evaluated olefin yields of diverse hydrocarbon mixtures, including polyolefins, crude oils, Fischer-Tropsch wax, and shale oil. To quantify the effects of pulse parameters on olefin production, we developed a spatiotemporal reactor model based on a quasi-molecular reaction network. The model reveals that pulsed Joule heating regulates high-temperature reactions to match product removal, thereby improving olefin yield and selectivity. Metal nanoparticles supported on carbon nanofibers (CNFs) are promising for catalytic and electrochemical applications, but controlling their size, dispersion, and phase during rapid thermal processing remains challenging. Here, we report a dual-solvent microwave carbothermal shock (CTS) method for producing Cu- and Ni-containing nanostructures on CNFs under ambient-pressure conditions. Ethanolic metal nitrate precursors were deposited on pristine CNFs, and hexane was introduced as an antisolvent before microwave irradiation. At 0.05 M Cu(NO3)2, hexane addition decreased the mean Cu-containing particle diameter from 50 ± 20 nm to 33 ± 12 nm and improved dispersion. Varying precursor concentration further altered particle morphology and aggregation. For Ni, single-solvent processing yielded aggregated nanoparticles averaging 43 ± 16 nm, whereas dual-solvent processing produced a dense carbon nanotube network with an apparent mean filament diameter of 20 ± 7 nm. Nitrate contamination of aquatic environments and the high energy and carbon intensity of conventional ammonia production represent two major and increasingly interconnected sustainability challenges. Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3RR) provides a compelling opportunity to address both by converting a widespread nitrogen pollutant into a value-added chemical and potential energy carrier under comparatively mild conditions. However, practical NO3RR remains constrained by sluggish multistep proton–electron transfer, competing hydrogen evolution, complex nitrogen-containing intermediates, and insufficient control over ammonia selectivity. High-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles have recently emerged as a promising catalyst platform for overcoming these limitations because their multielement compositions generate diverse adsorption sites, lattice strain, and tunable electronic interactions that can regulate the binding and transformation of key NO3RR intermediates. Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer-free catalyst layers based on custom-made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using O3 as counter-reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/IrOx and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 mg/cm2. The PEMWE cell-level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst-coated membrane anode despite 7x lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low-loading ALD-made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 mg/cm2.
